children: , the cloud and AI networking specialist, revealed that its multiyear purchase commitments had nearly tripled to $9.7 billion during Tuesday's Goldman Sachs conference. Shares were nearly flat Wednesday at $195.03, giving the company a market value of approximately $248 billion.

The demand is already reaching the income statement. Arista's second-quarter results delivered its first $3 billion quarter, with revenue surging 37.7% to $3.04 billion and adjusted operating margin hitting 49.9%. Management expects roughly $3.3 billion of third-quarter revenue, while new 1.6-terabit platforms position Arista to move even more data across sprawling AI clusters.

The $9.7 billion commitment figure equals about 3.2 quarters of current revenue, but investors should not mistake it for booked sales. Deployments can take 18 to 24 months while customers secure power, cooling, cabling and final approval, leaving Arista exposed to timing delays after it commits cash to inventory and suppliers. The picture reinforces that valuation risk: at $195.03, the stock trades 19.36% above its $163.39 GF Value, suggesting that plenty of AI-networking optimism is already priced in.

title: Arista's $9.7 Billion AI Commitments Hide an 18-Month Revenue Wait
